intro: FANN delivers clinic and medical-centre fit-out in Dubai and Abu Dhabi, including reception joinery, cabinetry, partitions and finishes. The proposed scope is reviewed around the actual facility, drawings, service interfaces and approval responsibilities.

sections.heading: Start with the actual facility brief
sections.text: Send the facility type, location, approximate area, existing condition and intended opening date. Add room layouts, equipment information and the drawings or BOQ available. Identify what is confirmed and what still needs design or technical input, so a quotation is based on the clinic you plan to operate.

sections.heading: Define approval and technical responsibilities
sections.text: Requirements vary by facility type and emirate. Bring the applicable landlord and authority information into the scope review and name who prepares submissions, coordinates the drawings and answers comments. Confirm the responsible technical parties and any specialist equipment interfaces. Do not treat a previous clinic project as approval for a new facility.

sections.heading: Release joinery against agreed details
sections.text: FANN has a joinery workshop in Umm Al Quwain. Review reception desks, storage and treatment-room cabinetry against the agreed drawings, materials, quantities and service interfaces before production. Changes to layouts, equipment or finishes need their effect on the scope and programme reviewed before the changed work proceeds.

sections.heading: Plan site checks and handover
sections.text: Agree the installation sequence, access arrangements and checks for the specified work. Record outstanding items and handover responsibilities, including information needed from other suppliers. The opening date, technical approvals and operating requirements should be coordinated as separate project inputs rather than replaced with a standard fit-out duration.

faqs.question: What information is needed for a clinic fit-out quote?
faqs.answer: Send the clinic location, approximate area, facility type, available drawings or BOQ and target opening date. Identify the rooms, equipment interfaces and landlord requirements already known. FANN can then review the fit-out scope and prepare a project-specific quotation, with inclusions, exclusions and unresolved inputs identified rather than assumed.

faqs.question: Are health-authority and landlord approvals included automatically?
faqs.answer: No. Approval requirements depend on the facility type, location and project. Share the applicable landlord and authority information, then agree who prepares each submission, coordinates the drawings and responds to comments. The proposal should identify those responsibilities. A fit-out quotation is not a guarantee of a particular approval outcome.

faqs.question: Can FANN produce clinic reception desks and cabinetry?
faqs.answer: Yes. FANN has a joinery workshop in Umm Al Quwain supporting the agreed clinic joinery scope. Review reception desks, storage and cabinetry against the approved drawings, materials, quantities and equipment interfaces before production. A previous reception photograph is a reference, not confirmation that the same detail suits your clinical requirements.

faqs.question: How should treatment-room services and finishes be coordinated?
faqs.answer: Review the room layout, equipment information and service requirements together before finishes or cabinetry are released. Identify the responsible technical parties, access needs and unresolved interfaces in the project scope. FANN coordinates the agreed fit-out work; the specific services, specialist equipment and checks need confirmation for the actual facility.

faqs.question: Can the opening date be confirmed before drawings are reviewed?
faqs.answer: No. A target opening date is an input to planning, not a confirmed fit-out duration. Drawings, specification, approvals, site access and equipment interfaces affect the programme. Share those inputs early, then confirm the agreed sequence and handover checks. Later changes need their effect on scope and timing reviewed before work proceeds.
